result:
I would remove the capacity to turn other conscious beings into abstractions.

Almost every large-scale cruelty—and plenty of quiet, everyday ones—depends on a specific mental shortcut: the ability to reduce another person’s vivid, complex inner life down to a category, a statistic, an obstacle, or background noise. It is how people justify wars, build exploitative systems, ignore suffering right in front of them, or say things online they could never say face-to-face.

It wouldn’t create a utopia. Scarcity, competing interests, grief, and genuine disagreements would still exist. People would still make mistakes and hurt each other out of desperation or clumsiness. 

But if it were impossible to stop feeling the full weight and reality of the person on the other side of an action, cruelty would lose its easiest hiding place. You would still have to solve hard problems, just without the convenient illusion that anyone else matters less than you do.
